summary: Texas does not make working smoke alarms a condition of selling a house; the state requirement attaches when a one- or two-family home is built, or when a permitted home improvement is done, and the only sale-specific rule is that a hearing-impaired buyer can require the seller to install special alarms before closing.
alarmType: The statute sets no technology or power source of its own. A one- or two-family dwelling constructed in Texas must have working smoke detectors installed per the smoke detector requirements of the building code in force in the local political subdivision, including its performance, location, and power source requirements. If the home does not comply, any home improvement needing a building permit must bring the smoke detectors up to that local code.
coAlarms: No statewide requirement for an existing one- or two-family home, at sale or otherwise, was found. The Health and Safety Code defines carbon monoxide alarm and directs the Texas Department of Insurance to publish public information about CO dangers and the availability of CO alarms, but imposes no installation duty. Local building codes may require them.
certification: No inspection or certificate. No fire department sign-off and no seller affidavit is required. Separately, the seller's disclosure notice a seller of residential real property must give the buyer has check boxes for Smoke Detector, Smoke Detector - Hearing Impaired, and Carbon Monoxide Alarm, so the seller states whether the home has them and whether they are in need of repair, but disclosing is not the same as having to install.
citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code ch. 766, subch. A, §§ 766.001-766.003 (requirement at construction, § 766.002; hearing-impaired alarms at sale, § 766.0021); Tex. Prop. Code § 5.008 (seller's disclosure notice); Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92, subch. F, §§ 92.251-92.260 (landlord smoke alarm duties, rentals only)
lastAmended: Chapter 766, Subchapter A was added by Acts 2007, 80th Leg., R.S., ch. 1051 (H.B. 2118), § 10, eff. September 1, 2007; no later amendment is shown on §§ 766.001-766.003.
notVerified: The statutes.capitol.texas.gov site is a JavaScript app and every direct page and document path returned only the app shell to curl. The statute text was read from the Legislature's own file server: https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/Zips/HS.htm.zip (file hs.766.htm) and https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/Zips/PR.htm.zip (files pr.5.htm, pr.92.htm).
Local building codes adopted by Texas cities and counties set the actual alarm specs and may add their own requirements at sale or at permit; no local ordinance was checked.
The exact wording and scope of the Property Code ch. 92 subch. F landlord duties was not read in full, only the section headings and the subchapter's placement in the residential tenancies chapter.
